platform: Windows, Intel Core i7-13620H; all new A/B timing collected on this one PC
clock: wall; do not combine absolute times with historical Mac thread-clock measurements

reasons: The fast path performs the same deterministic segment slice as the existing generic implementation, preserving the shared lower graph and accumulator. It adds no grammar restriction, approximate predicate, or persistent cache.

Dynamic JavaScript P90 improved in both independent Windows comparisons: 3.286 to 3.166 ms initially, and 3.293 to 3.167 ms with reversed process order. Same-binary disabled controls support attribution; earlier retained Mac comparisons also improved P90.

JavaScript stabilized P100 improved only slightly: 5.661 to 5.574 ms initially, and 5.666 to 5.656 ms in confirmation. This is not a major P100 breakthrough, and some intermediate tail quantiles remain worse.

All 8,332 llguidance-supported schemas were attempted in each native mode, with identical successes, failures, and 2,925,984 finite runtime interval keys. Dynamic native P100 decreased from 3.912 to 3.799 ms; static P100 decreased from 100.2 to 91.4 microseconds. Static build changes are small and mixed, not a compiler speedup claim.

The original 15.864 ms JavaScript and 75.6327 ms native-static spikes remain in the evidence. Neither recurred at its original coordinate in six fresh-process replays. Their causes are unproven. Confirmation raw JS maximum was still slightly higher for the candidate (6.913 versus 6.666 ms), as was the full native dynamic raw maximum; these observations are disclosed, not relabeled as fixed.

Thirty-two interleaved original-JS builds per variant did not reproduce the initial small build penalty: medians were 104.964 ms for baseline, 104.176 ms for the disabled control, and 103.203 ms for the default candidate. No build performance guarantee is made.

The Windows workspace library/integration suite passed 2,297 tests with zero failures and 55 ignored; all 42 Python tests and the documentation test passed. Four compiled/loaded static/dynamic streams each matched 77,582 complete masks across 126 schemas. Independent audits reconstructed the distributions, outcome coverage, and hashes from raw records. Loaded artifact byte variability occurred with the same two hashes in both binaries, with identical masks.
limitations: Strict P99-to-P100 dominance over llguidance is not achieved in the Windows empirical curves.
Raw wall-time maxima are not bounded by stabilized per-position minima; all original spikes remain in the published evidence.
Dynamic JavaScript compilation remains roughly 100 ms versus single-digit-millisecond llguidance builds in these measurements.

The unchanged optional Criterion benchmark expects 128,002 vocabulary entries and failed against the canonical 128,256-entry fixture; that failure is retained separately from the completed library/integration/doc/Python gates.
Other inconclusive runtime experiments are excluded; the separate bitmap compiler candidate is not part of this release.

js_curve_audit.definition: Independent sorted quantile curves on identical finite LL-measured keys. All linear-interpolation knots are checked. This describes measured samples, not a bound on future calls.

js_confirmation_curve_audit.definition: Independent sorted quantile curves on identical finite LL-measured keys. All linear-interpolation knots are checked. This describes measured samples, not a bound on future calls.

selection.selection: Top3 raw and top2 stabilized positions from each primary-screen dynamic variant, including LL; fixed before any replay. All original observations retained.

js_raw_replay.protocol: Six independent processes per mode, one fresh traversal per selected example; alternate execution order every round. All raw observations retained.

dynamic.selection: Union of top5 raw TBM, top3 stabilized TBM, and top3 minimum-build schemas from each complete original cohort. Selected before replay.

static.selection: Union of top5 raw TBM, top3 stabilized TBM, and top3 minimum-build schemas from each complete original cohort. Selected before replay.

js_dynamic_build_replay.purpose: Build-only confirmation; tiny example is an API/mask guard, not a runtime performance sample.

loaded_artifact_hash_replay.reason: Compiled artifacts match on all126 schemas; one loaded static artifact hash differed despite identical complete mask streams.

native_dynamic.metric: Native commit_i through mask_i+1; min of two complete observations per position
